sample.title: How The U.S Became So Dependent On Taylor Farms
sample.description:

After years of consolidation, experts say the company’s ability to control every stage of the supply chain has made it indispensable to grocers and restaurant chains, while raising the stakes for consumers when things go wrong. CNBC food and wellness reporter Brandon Gomez explains how the U.S. became so reliant on Taylor Farms.

sample.description:
At least 734 people have died and more than 2,400 people are missing in Nepal, local officials say, after flash floods on Wednesday, triggered by a glacier collapse.

Nearly 20,000 security forces are deployed in rescue efforts on the Nepal-Tibet border as the UN says rough terrain and rain is making aid delivery "extremely difficult”.

PC Andrew Harper's killers to stay in jail | BBC News Exclusive
sample.description:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has told the BBC that PC Andrew Harper's killers will remain behind bars as he announces changes to the early release scheme aimed at easing prison overcrowding. 

In an exclusive interview with BBC Breakfast, Burnham said anyone convicted of manslaughter will be excluded from changes brought in under the Sentencing Act, which would have made the killers eligible for early release. 

Burnham said extra prison spaces would be created by deporting "hundreds" of foreign prisoners and releasing some inmates serving indefinite sentences.

At least 37 dead in huge blast as arms depot hit by Russian drone in Ukraine | BBC News
sample.description:
37 people have been killed after a huge explosion at an arms depot in Ukraine which was struck by a Russian drone.  The ams storage facility was based near a residential areas on the outskirts of the capital, Kyiv.  Hundreds of people have been evacuated from the area and a rescue operation is continuing, with fears that the death toll will rise.

Shells, mines and drones stored at the facility exploded in a massive blast that destroyed nearby homes nearby, including a care home for the elderly and disabled. 

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky strongly criticised the location of the depot near people’s homes, saying an investigation had been launched into "terrible negligence on the part of those who stored explosive right next to people".

Russia's Ministry of Defence said that its forces had targeted "an ammunition depot”.

Ben Brown presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Dan Johnson in Kyiv.
